title: containerd leaks many <root>/tmpmounts/ovl-idmapped* mounts until restart
body:
### Description

containerd cleans up everything in tmpmounts when it starts up[0]. Starting with
1e3d10dc2 `("Make ovl idmap mounts read-only")`, at least on my systems, many more
mounts end up being leaked during containerd's lifecycle to the point where its a concern
in periods between restarting containerd.
```
# On a system that's been taking quick pods all night and is now empty
$ ls /tmp/ | grep ovl-idmapped | wc -l
0

$ ls /mnt/containerd/tmpmounts/ | grep ovl-idmapped | wc -l
2204

$ mount | grep tmpmounts | wc -l
2204

$ mount | grep ovl-idmapped | wc -l
2204
```

These are mounts made a part of `WithUserID()` while using user namespace enabled pods and come from containerd proper. The shims also make these sorts of mounts, but they're on `/tmp/` instead and don't end up leaking in my tests.

The mentioned commit seemed to have some background over [here](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/10955#discussion_r1833247757), where its also reported that @participant1 and @participant3 seemed to have similar issues, whereas @participant2 did not.

I for the life of me (i.e. an hour or two of poking around with bpf tools like opensnoop) can't figure out why *exactly* those mounts are reporting `-EBUSY` on my system, but they are with 2.1 and main. 

Leaking these mounts is bad as the mount table gets quite large, which can lead to large systemd slow downs, etc.

I'm wondering if we should prefer to go back to `MNT_DETACH`, or if we should add a retry mechanism on `-EBUSY` similar to other umount's in containerd? It seems hiding issues with `MNT_DETACH` isn't ideal, so maybe the latter is a safer bet.

For now on my systems I'm setting up a cron to clean up mounts in that folder that are considered "old enough", otherwise this would impact us too much.

[0]: https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/43f9cdd3bcf168c43ac0a2a3e4cfbd89610478ce/cmd/containerd/command/main.go#L180

### Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Run some user namespace enabled pods on containerd versions containing 1e3d10dc2 
2. Watch mounts hang around in `<root>/tmpmounts/ovl-idmapped*`


### Describe the results you received and expected

Very few if any mounts are leaked

### What version of containerd are you using?

v2.1.0-226-g43f9cdd3b 43f9cdd3bcf168c43ac0a2a3e4cfbd89610478ce

### Any other relevant information

_No response_

### Show configuration if it is related to CRI plugin.

_No response_

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Happy to make the PR for this, just looking for some guidance on if we think we should be retrying in the clean up functions, or if we should go back to MNT_DETACH, or add some GC loop, or some other option I'm not thinking of :D

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Thanks for the detailed report @reporter! I was personally in favor of leaving `MNT_DETACH` but I think we'd need consensus / sign-off for that. I'm also in theory interested in pursuing a solution where the idmap mounts are created and handed off to overlayfs without ever appearing in the systemwide mount table, but this requires very new kernels and if this is causing the issue you describe, it's probably worth thinking about a fix for older kernels too -- esp. if it could be as simple as MNT_DETACH.

We've been running this in production on fairly active hosts and haven't personally experienced this, but I think variability here is to be expected.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Well. MNT_DETACH will hide what real problem is.  So, `-10000000000000000000000000` for MNT_DETACH fro my side. 
We have a lot of discussion about MNT_DETACH and answer is NO. We can consider adding GC component for that.
However, I want to know how to make that mounpoint busy before any action. 
If there is any process scanning that folder, sorry, please turn it off or add that containerd in the skip-list or allowlist.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
@participant2 hear you loud and clear on the dislike for `MNT_DETACH`!

As for "who is using this and causing an -EBUSY", so far my attempts to find anyone opening that file path have not yielded anything. I'll find some more time to try and debug that further, or maybe there's more ways to cause a mount to report -EBUSY than simply having open fd's under the mount point (in which case my current searches would not have found those situations).

comments.author: participant3
reporter
comments.body:
@participant3 

>I guess if it happens, it might be slower to accumulate mounts (as we are doing only one mount instead of potentially a lot per rootfs), but I'm curious to know if it still happens.
> 
> If it happens, I think we need to debug to understand why. Furthermore, containerd is adding a garbage collector and mounts that we couldn't clean at the right time is a clear candidate for that.

It does still happen with those applied, but as you highlight we've got less bind mounts going on so the leakage is slower. I've been stress testing with those PRs a lot, and have canaried them to ~15 nodes in our cluster. I haven't hit any real issues outside of this one, and even then it was more of something I noticed at the time but didn't have any performance metric that was failing etc.

I'm sure if the nodes churned thru short lived pods for weeks (which is realistic for me) this could cause issues, hence my comment about adding a cron job for our nodes in the meantime while we sort this out. 

I do understand @participant2's point of "if you're doing something to cause this external of containerd, stop doing it". At the moment at least it doesn't seem to be anyone opening those paths (at least according to `opensnoop`), but I need to dig in more to see if something else is at play. The VFS code is tricky with the locks in my experience and I'm not exactly sure what all scenarios could cause an -EBUSY.

Okay, I could repro using the great repro from @participant1: https://github.com/containerd/containerd/issues/10704#issuecomment-2371949283. That repro also works to repro this issue :)

This issue was not happening with this PR applied: https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/10721 (the unmount with detach flag also fixes this).  But then PR https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/10955/ removed the detach and we started to leak the mounts as reported here.

@reporter @participant4 can you try PR #12114 and see if it fixes the problem for you?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Nice find @participant2 thanks for looking into this as well!

Are you saying that the ptraced process as part of `getUsernsFD()`
https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/cbe833eb4d664ac898282cce4c478617850f7aec/core/mount/mount_idmapped_utils_linux.go#L39
is to blame?

I went down that rabbit hole as well, but started to convince myself that because we don't set [ProcAttr::Files](https://pkg.go.dev/os#ProcAttr) that couldn't be it, but your comment makes sense. There's always a gap between fork() and execve(), and until the latter we don't close-on-exec any fd's, so this sounds likely to cause issues for any umounts we have a reference to when we fork for that.

Curious, did you manage to trace your way there, or just reason via looking at code? I failed to trace my way to that so far and would love to see how you did if you managed to, otherwise good catch on the code inspection, I convinced myself otherwise but this is a simple explanation and I'm glad you provided it.

Thanks again, this has literally been driving me crazy!

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Hi @reporter 

> Are you saying that the ptraced process as part of getUsernsFD()

Yes. For example,

| Timestamp | Goroutine 1 | Goroutine 2 | New Process X |
| :------- | :------: | -------: | ---:|
| T1  | FD = unix.OpenTree with OPEN_TREE_CLOEXEC  |   | | 
| T2 | MountSetAttr with IDMapping | Enter getUsernsFD and fork new process X | |
| T3 | MoveMount | ... | ...(holding FD) |
| T4 | close(FD) | ... | ... (holding FD ) |
| T5 | ... | ... | ... (holding FD) |
| T6 | umount temp mountpoint | ... | ... (holding FD) |
| T7 | log warning message - EBUSY | ... | execve |

> There's always a gap between fork() and execve(), and until the latter we don't close-on-exec any fd's, so this sounds likely to cause issues for any umounts we have a reference to when we fork for that.

Yeah. I think if we umount mountpoint created by OpenTree between fork() and execve(), it will be EBUSY. I don't know how to avoid it. It seems inevitable 😂  

> Curious, did you manage to trace your way there, or just reason via looking at code?

I used retsnoop as you did. Based on result, it has high reference number ([6]) before checking propagation. 
So, I think there are processes holding that file description of that mountpoint. 

```
↔ mnt_get_count        [6]        3.353us
```

I was suspecting systemd. But checking that code, found that systemd only read `/proc/self/mountinfo` without touching any mountpoint. I used bpftrace to check openat/mkdir/mkdirat but nothing. So I decided to use minimal test code to reproduce it. It's so crazy because I could't find anything wrong in code. After using `TestIDMapMountConcurrent` mentioned above, I can confirm that there could be kind of leaking file descriptor. So I spotted that unix.OpenTree fd and use `strace -f -e inject=execve:delay_enter=1000000:when=2` to delay syscall and found that. 😂 

It's so hard... anyway, we should use retry in whole codebase. 
Thanks for filing this issue. Learn so much things in this !

comments.body:
@participant2 great finding! And thanks for the table explaining the race! :)

That seems to be on spot, I've checked my setup and the `watch "mount | tail"` was not running inside the mntns, so that is why I wasn't seeing the leaks when running inside a mntns 🤦 . I corrected that and it indeed still leaks mounts when running the containerd daemon inside a mntns.

If the `mount()` method on Mount in mount_linux.go is called concurrently (I guess it is, but not sure atm), I think it will always be possible that one goroutine is doing the fork() while the other has an openfd that will cause the unmount to fail. It doesn't matter if we switch to `exec()` a new process (so the fd is closed) instead of ptrace it, the window might be smaller but it will still be there.

I agree the retry is the right fix for now (other clone flags don't seem nice), until the mount manager #11303 is merged and can handle this.
